lines.text: Lesson nine: fees, spread and slippage.
lines.say: Lesson nine: fees, spread and slippage.

lines.text: The small costs that can turn a win into a loss.
lines.say: The small costs that can turn a win into a loss.

lines.text: Here's a tiny trade: 0.01 BTC. The price on the chart goes from 60,000 to 60,080.
lines.say: Here's a tiny trade: zero point zero one B-T-C. The price on the chart goes from sixty thousand to sixty thousand eighty.

lines.text: On the chart, that looks like a gain of 0.80 USDT. Easy money?
lines.say: On the chart, that looks like a gain of zero point eight U-S-D-T. Easy money?

lines.text: Not so fast. Three costs are waiting: fees, spread and slippage.
lines.say: Not so fast. Three costs are waiting: fees, spread and slippage.

lines.text: A trading fee is charged each time an order fills, as a percentage of the position value.
lines.say: A trading fee is charged each time an order fills, as a percentage of the position value.

lines.text: Like a booking fee on a ticket: you pay it every time, whether things go well or not.
lines.say: Like a booking fee on a ticket: you pay it every time, whether things go well or not.

lines.text: 0.01 BTC at 60,000 is 600 USDT. At 0.05%, the fee is 0.30 USDT, on entry and again on exit.
lines.say: Zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand is six hundred U-S-D-T. At zero point zero five percent, the fee is zero point three U-S-D-T, on entry and again on exit.

lines.text: Many exchanges charge two rates. A taker order fills at once against the book, like a market order.
lines.say: Many exchanges charge two rates. A taker order fills at once against the book, like a market order.

lines.text: A maker order waits in the book, like a limit order, and adds to it. Makers often pay less.
lines.say: A maker order waits in the book, like a limit order, and adds to it. Makers often pay less.

lines.text: In this example: maker 0.02%, taker 0.05%. Real rates vary by exchange and account.
lines.say: In this example: maker zero point zero two percent, taker zero point zero five percent. Real rates vary by exchange and account.

lines.text: The spread is the gap between the best ask and the best bid.
lines.say: The spread is the gap between the best ask and the best bid.

lines.text: Like a money changer: one price to buy from them, a lower price to sell back.
lines.say: Like a money changer: one price to buy from them, a lower price to sell back.

lines.text: Ask 60,005, bid 59,995: spread 10. Buy and sell at once, and you lose 0.10 USDT on 0.01 BTC.
lines.say: Ask sixty thousand five, bid fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-five: spread ten. Buy and sell at once, and you lose zero point one U-S-D-T on zero point zero one B-T-C.

lines.text: Slippage, from T07: the fill is worse than the price you expected.
lines.say: Slippage, from T seven: the fill is worse than the price you expected.

lines.text: Say each market order slips 10 USDT per BTC, on the way in and on the way out.
lines.say: Say each market order slips ten U-S-D-T per B-T-C, on the way in and on the way out.

lines.text: That is 20 per BTC, or 0.20 USDT on 0.01 BTC.
lines.say: That is twenty per B-T-C, or zero point two U-S-D-T on zero point zero one B-T-C.

lines.text: Futures have one more cost: funding. It's a regular payment between long and short traders.
lines.say: Futures have one more cost: funding. It's a regular payment between long and short traders.

lines.text: It's separate from trading fees. You may pay it, or receive it, depending on the rate.
lines.say: It's separate from trading fees. You may pay it, or receive it, depending on the rate.

lines.text: Example: a 0.01% rate on 600 USDT is 0.06 USDT, each funding time. T13 covers it.
lines.say: Example: a zero point zero one percent rate on six hundred U-S-D-T is zero point zero six U-S-D-T, each funding time. T thirteen covers it.

lines.text: Now let's add it all up for our tiny trade.
lines.say: Now let's add it all up for our tiny trade.

lines.text: Chart gain: plus 0.80. Spread: minus 0.10. Slippage: minus 0.20.
lines.say: Chart gain: plus zero point eight. Spread: minus zero point one. Slippage: minus zero point two.

lines.text: Fees on entry and exit: minus 0.60 USDT.
lines.say: Fees on entry and exit: minus zero point six U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Net result: minus 0.10 USDT. A gross winner became a net loser.
lines.say: Net result: minus zero point one U-S-D-T. A gross winner became a net loser.

lines.text: Funding is left out here, because this trade was closed within minutes.
lines.say: Funding is left out here, because this trade was closed within minutes.

lines.text: The break-even move is how far price must move just to cover your costs.
lines.say: The break-even move is how far price must move just to cover your costs.

lines.text: Fees alone: 2 × 0.05% = 0.10%. On 60,000, that's 60 USDT per BTC.
lines.say: Fees alone: two times zero point zero five percent equals zero point one percent. On sixty thousand, that's sixty U-S-D-T per B-T-C.

lines.text: Add spread and slippage, and it's about 90 USDT per BTC, or 0.15%, before you make anything.
lines.say: Add spread and slippage, and it's about ninety U-S-D-T per B-T-C, or zero point one five percent, before you make anything.

lines.text: A common mistake: fees look tiny, so people ignore them.
lines.say: A common mistake: fees look tiny, so people ignore them.

lines.text: But 20 small trades at 0.60 USDT of fees each cost 12 USDT, win or lose.
lines.say: But twenty small trades at zero point six U-S-D-T of fees each cost twelve U-S-D-T, win or lose.

lines.text: Small, frequent trades feel the costs most. Count them before you trade.
lines.say: Small, frequent trades feel the costs most. Count them before you trade.

lines.text: Your turn. Buy 0.01 BTC at 60,000, sell at 60,040. Fees: 0.30 USDT on each side.
lines.say: Your turn. Buy zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand, sell at sixty thousand forty. Fees: zero point three U-S-D-T on each side.

lines.text: Ignore spread and slippage. What is the gross result, and the net? Pause if you need to.
lines.say: Ignore spread and slippage. What is the gross result, and the net? Pause if you need to.

lines.text: Gross: 40 × 0.01 = plus 0.40 USDT. Fees: 0.60. Net: minus 0.20 USDT.
lines.say: Gross: forty times zero point zero one equals plus zero point four U-S-D-T. Fees: zero point six. Net: minus zero point two U-S-D-T.

lines.text: A winner on the chart, a loser in your account.
lines.say: A winner on the chart, a loser in your account.

lines.text: Before any trade, check your real costs.
lines.say: Before any trade, check your real costs.

lines.text: Your actual fee rate and account tier. The spread right now. How deep the book is.
lines.say: Your actual fee rate and account tier. The spread right now. How deep the book is.

lines.text: The funding rate and time. And does the move you expect beat the break-even move?
lines.say: The funding rate and time. And does the move you expect beat the break-even move?

lines.text: If not, NO_TRADE is the sensible choice.
lines.say: If not, no trade is the sensible choice.

lines.text: This lesson used a simple model, with example numbers.
lines.say: This lesson used a simple model, with example numbers.

lines.text: Real fees depend on your exchange and account tier. Check them before you act.
lines.say: Real fees depend on your exchange and account tier. Check them before you act.

lines.text: Fees are charged on the full position value, not just the money you put in.
lines.say: Fees are charged on the full position value, not just the money you put in.

lines.text: And slippage grows in fast markets.
lines.say: And slippage grows in fast markets.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: Fees are charged on entry and exit, as a percentage of position value.
lines.say: Fees are charged on entry and exit, as a percentage of position value.

lines.text: Spread and slippage quietly worsen your prices. Funding is a separate futures cost.
lines.say: Spread and slippage quietly worsen your prices. Funding is a separate futures cost.

lines.text: Check yourself: the move you expect is smaller than the break-even move. What do you do?
lines.say: Check yourself: the move you expect is smaller than the break-even move. What do you do?

lines.text: Don't trade. Choose WAIT, or NO_TRADE.
lines.say: Don't trade. Choose wait, or no trade.

lines.text: Well done! That completes Phase 2. Next up, T10: a tour of an exchange platform.
lines.say: Well done! That completes Phase two. Next up, T ten: a tour of an exchange platform.
